subject: LuminaHealth onboarding: benchmark playbook & telemetry handoff
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Chen <echen@luminahealth.com>, Jack Ortiz <jack.ortiz@luminahealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: LuminaHealth onboarding: benchmark playbook & telemetry handoff

Hi Emily / Jack —

Thanks again for the sync yesterday. As discussed, attached is our initial benchmark playbook for the onboarding sprint. The goal for the pilot acceptance run is to validate latency and throughput targets on the Dedicated staging cluster so we can schedule the production rollout. Key items below — please review and confirm availability for the test window (week of Jan 18) and whether we can enable the staging endpoints described.

Targets and success criteria (proposal):
- Latency: p50 < 80ms, p95 < 240ms, p99 < 600ms for typical 256-token generation workloads
- Throughput: sustained 450 requests/sec with 99% success rate on a 6x GPU dedicated pool
- Tail/queueing: tail-latency incidents (10s+) must be resolved by autoscaling fallback within 30s
- Quality regression: generation quality checks using your seed prompts must not exceed a 6% divergence from baseline (we'll run a small eval set)

Planned artifacts (attached):
- lumina_loadplan_v1.xlsx: test matrix (concurrency, sequence lengths, warm-up cadence)
- telemetry_schema.json: fields we will collect (token counts, queue_time_ms, kernel_time_ms, kv_cache_hits)
- test_commands.sh: JMeter / k6 commands and sample payloads for the load harness

Operational notes:
- Endpoint: /private/lumina/v1/generate (staging) — we'll send an IAM key for access.
- Caching: we will enable prefix caching for common prompt prefixes; please flag any prompts with PII-sensitive content so we can exclude them from cached traces.
- Telemetry retention: default 14 days in staging; we can extend to 30 days on request for debug windows.

Action items:
1) Lumina: confirm test window (preferred Jan 18–20) and provide account IAM principal for staging access.
2) Redwood: we will provision the Dedicated pool and share stress harness commands once access is confirmed (Marcus will lead).
3) Security: if you want SOC2 artifacts or an evidence packet ahead of the run, indicate the owner and we will bundle it.

I'll follow up with a short runbook and schedule once I hear back.

Thanks —
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0137

Attachment: lumina_loadplan_v1.xlsx, telemetry_schema.json, test_commands.sh

Thanks Monica — quick clarifications before we lock the window.

> Hi Emily / Jack —
> 
> Thanks again for the sync yesterday. As discussed, attached is our initial benchmark playbook for the onboarding sprint. ...

Questions from our side:
- PII in traces: we need assurance that telemetry_schema.json excludes raw patient identifiers. Can you confirm that token-level traces will be scrubbed and that any stored prompts are hashed/partial?
- SOC2 / evidence: our security team needs the SOC2 Type II report and a short artifact (audit log sample) before the run.
- Test window: Jan 18 works for us but we have an internal release on Jan 19 morning — can we prioritize Jan 18 (US PST) for the heavy load and keep Jan 19 for a light follow-up?

Oliver from LoadLab (cc'd) is our performance consultant — he may coordinate the harness with Marcus.

Thanks,
Emily Chen
Director, Platform Engineering
LuminaHealth

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Chen <echen@luminahealth.com>, Jack Ortiz <jack.ortiz@luminahealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Oliver Grant <oliver@loadlab.io>
Date: Fri, 15 Jan 2027 11:55:00 -0800
Subject: Re: LuminaHealth onboarding: benchmark playbook & telemetry handoff

Emily / Jack / Oliver —

Thanks for the quick reply — below is a proposed ops-level schedule and the exact commands we'll run. Calls out where you need to sanitize prompts and where we purge telemetry.

Schedule (Jan 18, PST):
- 08:00–08:30: Provision & smoke test (health checks, warm caches)
- 08:30–10:30: Ramp to target (0 -> 450 rps over 15 minutes with 30m steady-state intervals)
- 10:30–11:00: Short pause for logs & sanity checks
- 11:00–12:30: Tail-latency sweep + failure-injection (circuit break) simulation
- 13:00–14:00: Quality eval run against seed prompts (non-PII set)

Endpoints and keys:
- Staging endpoint: https://staging-api.redwood.ai/private/lumina/v1/generate
- We will share a staging API key via the HubSpot secure notes (monica will provision)

Sample harness (k6):
- k6 run --vus 450 --duration 45m --rps 450 --env ENDPOINT=https://staging-api.redwood.ai/private/lumina/v1/generate --vus-scheduler --out json=lumina_jan18.json

If using JMeter, use the attached stress_commands.sh which contains JVM tuning flags and thread-group configs. Important: set the payload to the non-PII prompt set in the shared Drive folder (we'll add a read-only folder for Lumina).

Telemetry & privacy controls:
- Token traces: by default we capture token counts, model_time_ms, queue_time_ms and hashed prompt_id. We will not store raw prompt text for any prompt marked "PII" — those prompts will be redacted on ingestion.
- Audit logs: we will provide an audit-log sample (last 24h) to Lumina security before the run.
- Retention: staging telemetry will be kept for 14 days; we can extend to 30 days for post-mortem on request.

Attachments: stress_commands.sh (contains the exact k6/JMeter invocation / sampling scripts).

If that schedule looks good, Monica — please confirm and we'll provision keys + shared Drive folder by EOD Monday.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Principal SW Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai

Emily / Jack —

Great — Jan 18 is confirmed for the heavy run. Action checklist completed:
- Staging API key created and shared via HubSpot secure note (linked below)
- Read-only Drive folder created with non-PII prompt set and telemetry guidelines
- Stress harness commands deployed; Marcus has run a smoke pass with Oliver this morning
- SOC2 artifacts (Type II) and audit-log sample uploaded to the secure folder for your security team

We will perform the heavy ramp starting 08:30 PST on Jan 18; Redwood engineers will be on-call in the Slack channel #onboard-lumina for live triage. Please make sure your on-call perf/ops colleague is available at the start of the ramp.

Deliverables after the run:
- initial-results-summary.pdf (attached): includes throughput/latency graphs, error-rate breakdown by code path, and a list of any tail-latency incidents
- Raw telemetry export (lumina_jan18.json) uploaded to the shared Drive (14-day retention)
- HubSpot: updated deal notes and link to run artifacts (https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/LD-4932)

Next step: we'll do a findings review call Wednesday Jan 20 at 10:00 PST — invite coming from Laura. If anything blocks you before then ping me on Slack or reply to this thread.

Thanks everyone — excited to get this across the line.

Monica Patel
